summary: 1921 steel fire tower from Big Pocono State Park; taken down in 2017, restored at Grey Towers NHS in Milford, PA, and open on a trail there.

facts.design: Aermotor LS 40 steel tower with 7 by 7 foot cab
facts.status_note: Taken down at Big Pocono State Park in 2017 and moved to Grey Towers National Historic Site. A 40-foot replacement stands at the park.

staffing.status: mostly staffed in spring; fall depends on weather and need

access.note: Tower is on the Forest Discovery Trail at Grey Towers NHS. The 2017 plan said group access to the top cab would be supervised. Current rules not confirmed.

visit.trail_note: Half-mile Forest Discovery Trail behind the Grey Towers mansion. Ask the site about climbing before a visit.

facts.agency: USDA Forest Service at Grey Towers NHS; original owner Pennsylvania Bureau of Forestry

events.note: Built in 1921 per NHLR and the Forest Service; a 2017 Courier article says 1919
Disassembled in 2017 under Pennsylvania's fire tower upgrade
A 40-foot tower built in 2017 replaced it at Big Pocono State Park
Cut into two pieces and moved to Milford, to Grey Towers NHS
Cab restoration began in 2018; cab disassembled in summer 2018 and reassembled in summer 2019
Described in September 2022 as all but restored, with educational items still to finish; visitors could climb it during a festival

corrections.why: The 1921 tower was taken down in 2017 and moved to Grey Towers NHS. The tower standing at Big Pocono State Park is the 2017 replacement.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and the Forest Service give 1921; a 2017 Courier article says the tower was first installed in 1919. The story uses 1921.
The register and Grey Towers give 21 ft; a 2017 Courier article gives 35 ft and does not say how it measured. The record uses 21 ft (6.4 m).

notes_for_editor: Current climbing rules and whether the 1921 tower is open today are unverified; newest source is September 2022. The record's coordinates point to Big Pocono State Park, where the 2017 replacement stands; the 1921 tower is at Grey Towers (Milford), and no source here gives coordinates for it, so the point was not changed. Height: register and Grey Towers say 21 ft, Courier 2017 says 35 ft; height_m 6.4 is converted from 21 ft. The NHLR 2017 entry lists 'Built 1921' for the replacement tower, which looks like a copy error. No notable fire found.
